killXP._comment: What ONE mob death pays ONE participant (docs/archive/plan-xp-formula.md). Anchored to the RECIPIENT's level, not the mob's: award = base(P) × mod(Δ) × tier × the mob's authored xpFactor, where base(P) = base × growth^(P−1). growth == levelUpXPGrowthFactor is what makes kills-per-level flat across the span (~7.5 at these numbers); dropping it below is the one knob that slows the late game. Δ ≥ 0 pays +upBonusPerLevel per level up to upBonusCapLevels — that bound is what stops a carried low-level player levelling off an endgame kill. Δ < 0 tapers linearly, but the gray boundary (grayBase + P/grayStep levels below you) TRUNCATES the taper while it still pays ~1 − 1/taperStretch of an at-level kill — the taper's own zero sits taperStretch× deeper (D13, WoW Classic's two-distance shape; sub-1 values clamp to 1). At/past the boundary a kill pays exactly 0, which is what stops endgame gray farming. Normal has no multiplier by design: base IS the at-level normal kill. ⚑ A field left out (or set ≤ 0) falls back to the Go default FOR THAT FIELD — so authoring only base+growth does not zero the gray distance or the tier weights. The flip side: **`upBonusPerLevel` and `upBonusCapLevels` cannot be authored as 0** (WoW-flat, no bonus for killing above your level) — they would read as unauthored. Expressing that needs pointer conf fields; C2's problem if it ever wants it. A genuinely free species is `xpFactor: 0`, never a zeroed tier. ⚑ The Go defaults in pkg/aura/curve (DefaultKillXP) are the source of truth; this restates them, and removing the block resolves back to them rather than zeroing the economy. All values [PLACEHOLDER] — C2 calibrates against the simharness kills-per-level battery.

mob._comment: Stats mobs share with the player block, same names + same units (backlog §27.2.3). healthGainTick is out-of-combat regen as a fraction of the max pool per tick; 0.006666667 = full pool in 5 s (PO 2026-07-26) — the exact float32 decimal of the Go default 1/150, so the restatement is bit-exact (§35 C1; the old 0.0066667 was a rounded copy that resolved a hair off the confs with no mob block). walkingSpeedPerTick is the base movement step multiplied by each mob's factors.speed — same name and unit as the player's, deliberately NOT the same value (0.055 vs 0.05; every authored factors.speed is tuned against it — plan-entity-model.md L1). The Go defaults in model/mob are the source of truth for both; this restates them, and removing an entry resolves back to it. NOTE: vitals.HP floors a step at 1 HP, so pools under ~150 refill in maxHealth/30 s regardless. [PLACEHOLDER]
mob._comment_dormancy: wakeMargin/sleepMargin size mob DORMANCY's wake volume (plan-world-scale.md S3, D6) as dimensionless multiples of the 20x12 AOI box — NOT distances in units. A mob wakes inside wakeMargin x AOI and sleeps only outside sleepMargin x AOI; the gap is the anti-thrash hysteresis band. The volume itself is derived from constant.ViewPortWidth/Height at the read site, so it tracks the viewport automatically. Awake mob count scales with the SQUARE of the margin, so every doubling costs 4x (the rejected hand-set 40-unit radius woke ~235 mobs/player and capped the server at ~7 dispersed players). sleepMargin is THE perf knob and wakeMargin is the safety knob: a woken mob does not sleep again until it leaves the SLEEP box, so that box sets the steady-state awake population (measured 2026-08-30 at 14 640 mobs: 2.2 -> 1.9 is -26% awake and -17% tick time, consistently from 10 to 150 players; it moves the mob subsystem ceiling from ~75 to ~100 dispersed players). Invariants, guardrail-asserted in cmd/simharness: wakeMargin > player.FlightViewportScale (NOT > 1 - a FLYING player streams a scaled-up AOI, and that, not the ground viewport, is the box the wake volume must contain) and sleepMargin > wakeMargin (hysteresis is a band, not an inversion; the band is what a player must walk to toggle a mob). Absent resolves to these values. [PLACEHOLDER]
